newsitem.title: MEXICO: GCC says dumping margin was 26 pct.
newsitem.headline: GCC says dumping margin was 26 pct.

text.p: Grupo Cementos de Chihuahua estimated that its dumping margin over the period between July 1994 and August 1995 was about 26 percent, or well below the 42.74 percent tariff levied on the company's exports to the United States, a top company official told Reuters on Friday.
"We were paying a tariff of 42.74 percent (per tonne) exported during the fifth administrative period (July 1994-August 1995)," said Jaime Fernandez, Chief Financial and Planning Officer at GCC.
"But we estimate that our margin was around 26 percent," he added.
In September, the U.S. Department of Commerce raised its anti-dumping tariff to 107.8 percent in a preliminary review of the period in question.

"Although it is not final, we reckon that our dumping margin, even calculated using U.S. criteria, is 26 percent, for which reason we may be reimbursed, with interest, as of June 1997," Fernandez added.
The review for the fifth period ends in April 1997.
"The most they can raise the anti-dumoping tariff to is 90 percent, as an average for Cemex and ourselves, but not to 107.8 percent," he said.
GCC will report its third quarter earnings on October 21, Fernandez said.
